speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome. I see you are a newborn with feeding intolerance and bilious vomiting; have you noticed any abdominal distension or signs of bilious material in your stool? This is critical as bilious vomiting in a newborn can indicate a surgical emergency like malrotation with volvulus.

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, 3050-g (6-lb 12-oz) male, six hours post delivery. The newborn has had several episodes of bilious vomiting and is intolerant to feeding since birth. Was born at term following an uncomplicated pregnancy, though the mother missed several prenatal checkups. The patient's older brother underwent surgery for pyloric stenosis as an infant.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your brother's history of pyloric stenosis, could you confirm if your mother noticed a visible peristaltic wave or a palpable "olive" mass in your abdomen? Additionally, have you passed any meconium within the first 48 hours of life?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Bilious vomiting. I also have Feeding intolerance, No fever, Vomiting started within first day after birth.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Malrotation with Volvulus.

REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal Ultrasound, Upper Gastrointestinal Series.
REQUEST TEST: Electrolytes.

Please confirm if the GI series shows a "corkscrew" appearance of the duodenum, as this would confirm the diagnosis.
